cues: At a conservatory audition, the applicant performs Haydn’s E-flat concerto, a standard showcase for nimble upper-register playing.
In Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto No. 2, a specialist carries the demanding clarino line above the strings.
In Mahler’s Fifth Symphony, an opening solo sounds from offstage before the orchestra begins its funeral march.
During the Beatles’ recording of “Penny Lane,” a high piccolo part adds a baroque flourish to the melody.
At a Miles Davis retrospective, listeners hear how the jazz innovator’s lead playing helped shape modern jazz.
On a Louis Armstrong tribute program, a player recreates the buoyant lead style heard in early New Orleans jazz.
